scorecard.note: Add a verifiable source for the percentage and growth figures to avoid invented facts.

storyboard.ears: The web diversified fast, yet English kept a narrower lead.
English fell to 45% of web pages by 2005. The early web was no longer overwhelmingly English.
storyboard.evidence: UNESCO-affiliated web language monitoring report | English-language share of web pages | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_used_on_the_Internet | 2026-09-12

storyboard.ears: Arabic online content grew 2,501% over the measured decade. Other languages expanded far faster than English.
storyboard.eyes: substance: lines of Arabic script; cause: Data hammers the laptop's keys and every strike writes more lines of Arabic onto the screen
storyboard.evidence: Internet World Stats, cited in UNESCO multilingualism research | Growth in online content by language, 2001-2011 | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Languages_used_on_the_Internet | 2026-09-12

storyboard.ears: English now appears on 55% of websites. It still leads, but no longer monopolizes the web.
storyboard.evidence: W3Techs | English's share of websites today vs every other language combined | https://w3techs.com/technologies/overview/content_language | 2026-09-12

storyboard.ears: Browsing beyond English now opens a large part of the modern web.
